title: How do we draw a trapezium with a chosen area?
description: A trapezium has the same area as a rectangle as tall as the trapezium and as long as half the sum of its parallel sides. So we choose a rectangle of area one hundred forty four square centimetres, read off the height and the sum of the parallel sides, and pick two sides that add up to it.
teaching_notes: One idea: a trapezium has the area of a rectangle of the same height and half the sum of the parallel sides, so we can work backwards from a chosen rectangle. Watch for students who think only one trapezium can have the given area.

source: Construct a trapezium of area 144 cm2 using the idea of converting a trapezium into a rectangle of equal area and back
video_script.why: The child knows the rule for the area of a trapezium and now works backwards from a chosen rectangle to the sides of a trapezium.
video_script.substitution: A rectangle of twelve by twelve and the parallel sides eight and sixteen are one choice among many.
video_script.anchor: a rectangle twelve centimetres by twelve centimetres that turns into a trapezium of the same area
video_script.payoff_line: Make the parallel sides eight and sixteen centimetres. Make the height twelve centimetres.

final_answer.value: parallel sides 8 cm and 16 cm, height 12 cm
final_answer.spoken: parallel sides of eight and sixteen centimetres, with a height of twelve centimetres

maths_rules: area of a trapezium = 1/2 x h x (a + b) = h x (1/2 x (a + b)), the area of a rectangle with sides h and 1/2 x (a + b)
choose a rectangle of area 144: 12 x 12 = 144, so h = 12 and 1/2 x (a + b) = 12, so a + b = 24
any h and a + b with h x (a + b) = 288 works
video_script.design: A twelve by twelve rectangle stays on the board. The rule is written once, the height and the sum of the parallel sides are read off, and a trapezium with those sides is drawn on top of the rectangle.

<bookmark mark='area'/>We have to draw a trapezium that covers one hundred forty four square centimetres.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Many trapeziums will do, but we need only one. What must we choose?

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: a trapezium with parallel sides a and b and height h turns into a rectangle with height h and length 1/2 × (a + b); the rule area = 1/2 × h × (a + b) is written

beats.moves_through: the trapezium turns into the rectangle
narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>We use the same way as the example in your book. Area is half times the height times the sum of the parallel sides.
<bookmark mark='rect'/>This is the area of a rectangle. The rectangle is as tall as the trapezium, and as long as half the sum.

marks.given: the words area 144 cm² are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the area is one hundred forty four square centimetres.

beats.on_screen: To find: parallel sides a and b and a height h for a trapezium

marks.find: the words parallel sides a and b and height h are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to choose the two parallel sides and the height.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: choose a rectangle of area 144 cm²: 12 × 12 = 144

marks.rect: a rectangle 12 cm by 12 cm appears

narration: <bookmark mark='rect'/>Step one, choose a rectangle with the same area.
<bookmark mark='val'/>Twelve by twelve works, because twelve times twelve is one hundred forty four.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: height h = 12; half of (a + b) = 12, so a + b = 2 × 12 = 24

marks.height: h = 12 is written on the side of the rectangle
marks.len: half of (a + b) = 12 is written on the other side
marks.sum: a + b = 2 × 12 = 24 is written under it

narration: <bookmark mark='height'/>Step two, the height of the trapezium is twelve.
<bookmark mark='len'/>Half the sum of the parallel sides is also twelve.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>The sum is two times twelve, twenty four.

marks.pick: a = 8 is written for the top side
marks.other: b = 24 - 8 is written for the bottom side

narration: <bookmark mark='pick'/>Step three, choose any top side that is less than twenty four. Let it be eight centimetres.
<bookmark mark='other'/>The two sides must add up to twenty four. The bottom side is twenty four take away eight.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: check, 1/2 × 12 × 24: half of 12 is 6, and 6 × 24 = 144

marks.rule: the rule is written with h = 12 and a + b = 24
marks.val: 6 × 24 = 144 is written and matches the area asked for

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step four, put the numbers back into the rule. Half times twelve times twenty four.
<bookmark mark='val'/>Half of twelve is six, and six times twenty four is one hundred forty four. That is the area we wanted.

beats.on_screen: Answer: parallel sides 8 cm and 16 cm, height 12 cm; area 144 cm²

marks.ans: the trapezium with parallel sides 8 cm and 16 cm and height 12 cm is drawn and boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Make the parallel sides eight and sixteen centimetres. Make the height twelve centimetres.
<bookmark mark='area'/>This trapezium covers one hundred forty four square centimetres. Other choices work too, if the height times the sum of the sides is two hundred eighty eight.
